title: Peace and Loss
subtitle: Can I see a falling tear, and not feel my sorrow's share?

items.text: Peace and Loss
The ceiling hangs overhead like the cold sky on a winter's day.
Yet her body, gently cocooned in blankets, feels warm.
Ward, Rehab Center

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Where-Where am I? Merel?
Just as Mama foretold, she wakes at a time long since set in stone.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Matilda, you're awake.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Vertin, Sonetto? Wh-What are you doing here?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Madame Bouanich predicted you'd wake up sometime today, so we thought we'd drop by. I'm sure you want to hear about the school.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Mama is here? No, then the "Storm" has passed? The school—
She grimaces from a piercing pain in her brow.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: The students are safe. Most of them made it through.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: "Most"? And Merel?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: *sigh* We'll talk more once you're feeling better.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: I'm perfectly fi—ah.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You need to rest. Just lie down for now. Your mother will be here soon.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: How long has she been back at headquarters?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: She came as soon as the "Storm" ended. She barely left your side up until now.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: The Foundation needed her for some paperwork. She should be back any moment.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: She brought you a new crystal orb to replace the one you lost during the fight.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Hngh.
She tries to turn to look at the gift at her bedside, but the neck brace denies her.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Please, don't get up. The doctor said you need to rest for now.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We've got a few more "get well" presents for you. Probably easier if we show them to you.
A Shelter Dove

branch.speaker: Matilda
branch.text: A Shelter Dove? Goodness! Th-That is not something you should just be carrying around like a toy.

branch.speaker: Vertin
branch.text: It's only a replica the students made. Plug it into a 230-volt outlet, and it lights up. More of a lamp than a shelter.

branch.speaker: Vertin
branch.text: Lavender brought it over when she came to visit. She said the students are all wishing you a quick recovery.

branch.speaker: Matilda
branch.text: A lamp? It-It looks so much like the real thing.

items.text: Rider-Waite Tarot Cards

branch.speaker: Vertin
branch.text: Sonetto and I thought you'd appreciate this.

branch.speaker: Matilda
branch.text: Oh, my heart! You did this on purpose, just to tease me, no? Tell me you didn't forget what I actually use for divination.

branch.speaker: Vertin
branch.text: Of course not, which is precisely why we picked one with silly anecdotes on arcanum on the back.

branch.speaker: Vertin
branch.text: You can read it like a storybook.

branch.speaker: Matilda
branch.text: Hmph. Then I suppose it isn't all that bad.

items.text: Super Chips with Zesty Salsa
items.edge_label: 超大份玉米片与墨西哥辣酱组合套餐

branch.speaker: Matilda
branch.text: Super chips with zesty salsa? Don't tell me they're from—

branch.speaker: Vertin
branch.text: J? Yes. He went to great lengths to sneak them in.

branch.speaker: Matilda
branch.text: Chips? He's hopeless. What on earth must go through that big head of his?

items.text: End Conversation
Continue

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Just leave the rest. I'll look through them myself once I can move a bit more easily. It shouldn't be more than a few days.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Until then, I will lie here and think about how to repay their kindness, properly.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Of course. We'll leave you to it.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Laplace wants to see me as soon as possible. We'll visit again soon.

items.speaker: Letter of Appointment
items.text: "With heavy hearts, we announce the passing of Richard Schafer, Principal of the SPDM."

items.speaker: Letter of Appointment
items.text: "The Joint Committee of St. Pavlov Foundation has elected to appoint Zhāng Zhīzhī as Acting Principal until further arrangements can be made. This decision is effective immediately."

items.speaker: Letter of Appointment
items.text: "Her existing responsibilities will remain unchanged."
She takes a sip of her soon-to-be lukewarm tea. A scarlet berry dissolves in her mouth.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: You look as stunned as the day I named you chief of staff.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: You had that tea back then, too. Has it always been the same blend? Milkvetch, goji berries, ginseng? Or was it dong quai?

items.speaker: Z
items.text: The latter, along with a few other herbs. It was a gift from Black Ibis.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: Ma'am, forgive me for repeating what I said back then, but I fear I may not be the right person for the job.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: The SPDM has been asking for their principal to be put on the Joint Committee for a while now.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: This makes for a convenient workaround. We put a Committee member as their principal.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: With respect, ma'am, I haven't been involved in school affairs for years. Many will doubt the decision.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: I wouldn't be concerned about that. We've got more than enough justification to back this appointment.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: Had Vertin and Sonetto not uncovered the secret of the "boon," every student in that library would have been exposed to the "Storm." It's as sound a reason as any for you, their direct supervisor, to assume office.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: On top of that, Investigator Matilda placed herself in grave danger, and Ms. Merel gave her life protecting the students. The Timekeeper's team paid a heavy price to compensate for the school's failures. I am confident they will accept the matter with grace.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: Merel ... Merel Van der Veer.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: I only spoke to her once, before she left for Antarctica. She never seemed to want the spotlight.
She walks through her brief memories of their meeting, contemplating what she can say about the girl.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: She was happy just being an ordinary girl.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: Whether she'd have liked it or not, her name will be remembered by those students for the rest of their lives.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: Without her, the spare Doves would have never gotten to the library. Those kids would have been lost before the Timekeeper returned.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: The "Storm" Fallen Employees Archive will preserve her medal permanently.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: When you get to the school, the first priority will be reconstruction. Nearly its entire staff was wiped out. They'll be desperate for new blood.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: That sounds very much like the Foundation right now.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: We took our share of losses—experienced staff who had survived multiple "Storms," some went all the way back to before the first.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: Have you read Ms. Stranger's report, ma'am?
She lifts her cup again. It's cold.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: Yes. If you're curious how Manus Vindictae slipped its troops in here unnoticed, it was through something they call the "Windweave."

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: Ms. Stranger discovered a portal and, within it, a gigantic beast thought to be the Manus troops' carrier. She believes someone inside the Foundation opened the portal and guided the Manus here.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: The captive ritualist's testimony supports this theory.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: But who was their accomplice inside the Foundation?
Hallway, Laplace

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Vekiĝu en la regno de mortemuloj.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Slow down. What's the hurry? A dog chasing you or something?

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: A dog? More like three Critters in a lab coat who keep yapping at me. We might as well throw the Workplace Noise Regulations straight in the trash.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: In all fairness, Adler, you never specified the speed or cadence of the incantation—a flaw in our experiment protocol, I'd say. I thought you'd have established more stringent guidelines after the ninth "Storm."

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Ah, yes, how very helpful of you, Ulrich.
Laplace's scientists are on high alert, as usual.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Mr. Enigma.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Timekeeper, you've arrived at the perfect moment.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Am I interrupting? Looks like you're experimenting with that incantation I learned from the "boon."

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Yes. We hear you haven't suffered any adverse effects from reciting the incantation. Quite the difference from the "first circle" situation.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: If we can decode the mechanics behind this incantation, we may be able to significantly improve the effectiveness of our anti-"Storm" equipment.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Yes, provided the incantation actually works.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: After our Awakened colleagues confirmed the incantation's harmlessness on them, we gathered subjects of every race we could find at Laplace: human, arcanist, even artificial intelligence.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: These dorks even tried to find a "female arcanist of the Timekeeper's age" in an attempt to control the variables. Ha, like that would ever work.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: I told you, didn't I? Vertin's one of a kind!

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: As you can see, Timekeeper, we need your assistance. Could you please recite the incantation while connected to our energy monitoring systems?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: How do I connect to your system? Do I need to wear a monitoring device?

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: No need. The systems in this hallway have already linked up to you.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I see.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Vekiĝu en la regno de mortemuloj.
The clamor of the Laplace hallway drowns the voice out.
Perhaps it's due to the lack of the "boon" as a medium, or perhaps it's due to the "Storm's" environmental factors, but ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Nothing's happened.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: This is it.
The Committee members look out over Building 5.
Warning tape blocks access to the once normal building. Only select staff members donning protective gear are permitted entry.

items.speaker: Operation Team Leader I
items.text: Keep clear. Building 5 is temporarily closed. Authorized personnel only.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: This is where the largest breach occurred. Of course, all traces of the portal are gone now. Ms. Stranger sealed it completely.
They look up at the crumbling tower, standing tall at the center of a vacuum sealed off by a cordon.
An arcanist architect has stabilized it, but the loose rubble still falls from time to time.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: Ms. Cornerstone is overseeing the building's repairs. But the greater concern right now is our looming staff shortage.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: It seems that we have no choice but to keep expanding admissions. The Resolution must stay in effect.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: But, didn't you say it was the cause of this incident?

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: Yes. The Resolution undoubtedly intensified the long-lasting resentment against our refugee policy. Many were upset by our decision, and it seems that agitation escalated into treason.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: The Foundation has always had to make difficult decisions in regard to who we grant refuge to. Every one of us has been forced to watch family and friends perish in the "Storm."

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: Even among those we do save, many join us unaware of the true ramifications of the "Storm" and the devastation that comes with it.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: But in this last era, Manus Vindictae revealed the existence of the "Storm" to a larger population than ever before. Once we passed the Resolution, it was all but certain that we would be flooded with refugees.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: And yet we couldn't let them all in. It wasn't fair, of course, but fairness isn't a luxury we can afford.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: No matter how much we expand, we still can't shelter everyone.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: Then do you believe this was done in retaliation to the Foundation's strict admission policy?

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: It isn't quite that simple. The staff involved seemed to be acting out of conscience, not resentment. They thought, for whatever reason, that they were doing the right thing.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: These are wounded, traumatized people, tormented for years by the grief and anxiety of living out of their own time.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: When they saw the desperate crowd outside the gates, they could only think of their own friends and families.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: Lyra saw her chance and took advantage of their sympathy.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: She promised them a way to save more people. If they helped create a passage bypassing Foundation security, all those waiting outside could take refuge from the "Storm."

items.speaker: Z
items.text: None of them expected Arcana would be the one coming through that portal.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: No. They never meant for this to happen. But good intentions can still lead to catastrophe.
The politicians fall silent. Who would be fit to judge them by their intentions?

items.speaker: Z
items.text: So, what do we do with them?

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: What would you do if it were your decision?

items.speaker: Z
items.text: Given the number of people involved, strict punishment would only further destabilize our already fragile situation.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: Perhaps we can give them a chance to make it right: send them into the field to go after Lyra and investigate this "Windweave."

items.speaker: Z
items.text: They've already paid dearly for their actions. I doubt anyone will fall for her words again.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: Moreover, they've had firsthand experience with the "Windweave." At this moment, there's unlikely anyone more suitable than them to look for it.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: I'll take it under consideration. It may well be the most practical solution, and I'm sure the court will agree.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: I have two direct requests from Vertin: one asking permission to return to her field duties, and the other is about Ms. Stranger.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: But, since she belongs to the Secondary Defense Program, it falls outside my authority to make the decision.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: The Timekeeper wants Ms. Stranger to be released from all her current duties and put under her team.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: Ms. Stranger has explicitly stated that she has no desire to restore her Phototaxis and wishes to keep all her current memories. She hasn't decided on the other aspects of her work yet.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: Let her keep them. To have rejected the mask and survived—that alone proves her loyalty.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: What about her other requests?

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: You're asking me to give up the program's strongest asset.
Constantine doesn't continue her questioning. She pauses, reflecting on her subordinate's reply.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: I thought she'd prefer to forget it all.
